headline: Maui County Committee on the Status of Women

meeting.body: Maui County Committee on the Status of Women
meeting.summary: The committee voted to send a midwifery legislation letter to legislators toward the end of November and moved its budget vote to the next meeting.
meeting.recap: A home birth task force chair asked that the letter to legislators back three changes to midwifery law.[[0:04:38]] She asked that the letter go to every state representative and senator after the November election.[[0:05:26]] An apprentice Hawaiian birth keeper testified in support of the committee's letter backing midwifery legislation.[[0:51:44]] Members took a voice vote on accepting the draft letter as written.[[1:16:36]] Members voted unanimously to attach the bill and two past committee letters to the letter.[[1:18:53]] Members voted unanimously to send the letter to legislators toward the end of November.[[1:26:02]] The same motion has the letter go to the women's caucus as soon as possible.[[1:26:02]] The budget vote is planned for the next meeting.[[1:28:39]] The chair deferred the remaining agenda items to the next meeting.[[1:42:07]]
decided: Members voted unanimously to attach the bill and the committee's past letters to the letter.
Members voted unanimously to send the letter to legislators toward the end of November and to the women's caucus as soon as possible.
Members agreed to vote on the budget at the next meeting.
The chair deferred the rest of the agenda items to the next meeting.
meeting.next: The vice chair will provide the women's caucus contact so the letter can be sent as soon as possible. A member agreed to help the chair build the list of legislators after the election. Members will email the issues important to them so the secretary can put them in a spreadsheet before the next meeting.

moments.q: Home birth task force chair lists three points for the letter
